messages:
Elena (People Ops): FYI vendor payout issue - contractor Asha Patel (vendor id V-7721) got paid through payroll on 2026-02-20 instead of AP. She received net deposit and was taxed. We need to untangle 1099 vs payroll tax withholding. @Omar @Priya
Omar (Payroll): Oof. Emp-like payment posted under one-off paycode CNTR_PAY on PR-2026-02-20-04. Give me vendor id / last4 if you have it.
Elena (People Ops): Vendor id V-7721, last4 bank 1199. Gross payment $3,200. Payroll Bot journal extract:
```PR-2026-02-20-04
DR Payroll Expense 3200
CR Cash 2400
CR Fed_Withholding 352
CR State_Withholding 192
CR SS_FICA 256```
Priya (Accounts Payable): That should have been an AP invoice — V-7721 submitted invoice INV-2026-0119 for $3,200 flagged as contractor. Looks like invoice was routed to payroll by mistake during month-end.
Omar (Payroll): So payroll withheld federal/state and payroll taxes which is wrong for a contractor. If we leave as-is, it will show on a W-2 for the payroll account. Correct approach: reverse payroll posting, issue AP payment via ACH with no withholdings, and ensure 1099-NEC is issued for V-7721.
Jason (Tax Counsel): Agreed. Also check backup withholding rules: did vendor provide W-9? If not, we may owe backup withholding (24%) and 1099-BK? But for missing TIN we'd have withheld at 24%. Do we have a W-9 on file?
Priya (Accounts Payable): We have W-9 dated 2025-06-10 with TIN on file. No backup withholding required.
Omar (Payroll): Plan: 1) Create reversing payroll adjustment PR-ADJ-2026-03-12 to remove gross and tax liabilities and refund the withheld taxes to company tax liabilities. 2) Issue vendor payment AP-2026-03-15 for $3,200. 3) Adjust federal/state deposit records and file Form 941-X or state equivalents if deposits already sent. 4) Ensure 1099-NEC for 2026 includes this invoice.
Payroll Bot: Reverse preview journal PR-ADJ-2026-03-12:
```DR Fed_Withholding 352
DR State_Withholding 192
DR SS_FICA 256
DR Cash 2400
CR Payroll Expense 3200
CR Payroll_Liability_Adjust 0```
Elena (People Ops): Will the vendor need any outreach about the mispayment and timing? She already messaged HR confused about taxes taken.
Priya (Accounts Payable): I'll draft an outreach note to Asha explaining we'll reissue payment via AP on 3/15 and provide a summary of withheld amounts we reversed for accounting. We'll include timeline and offer a proof-of-payment letter.
Jason (Tax Counsel): One more: if we already included amounts on Form 941 for Q1 deposits, we must file 941-X to correct employer deposits and explain recovery of withheld amounts. Omar, coordinate with Finance for deposit timelines.
Omar (Payroll): Noted. I'll open case PAY-CASE-7054 with attachments: payroll journals, AP invoice, W-9. Estimated timeline: reversing entry and AP pay within 5 business days; 941-X prep in parallel with Finance and Tax. If vendor already received net and spent it, we still need to correct books — but no action required from vendor other than confirmation of new ACH.
Elena (People Ops): Thanks. Please copy me on vendor note and add a plain-language FAQ for future mistaken routing. We should also check process to prevent payroll routing for AP-coded invoices.
Priya (Accounts Payable): Agreed. I'll add an invoice routing rule to block invoices with contractor tag from going to payroll queue and add a monthly QA spot-check.
Payroll Bot: Case PAY-CASE-7054 created. Attachments: INV-2026-0119, PR-2026-02-20-04 journal, W-9_V-7721.
Jason (Tax Counsel): Approved remediation steps. Let's proceed and keep audit trail.
Omar (Payroll): I'll post PR-ADJ-2026-03-12 today after approvals and schedule AP-2026-03-15. Will update this thread when complete.
Elena (People Ops): Great, thanks team. I'll follow up on the process change and share the draft vendor message here for review before sending.
